items.title: A more tailored Google Search that’s uniquely yours
items.body:
Get more helpful Search responses by securely opting in to connect Google Wallet, Drive, and the Gemini app to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode.

Your browser does not support the audio element.

We’re adding Google Wallet and Drive to Personal Intelligence, allowing Search to provide answers based on your spending, documents, and chats. These updates help you manage finances, organize projects, and maintain context across your search threads. You can opt in to connect these apps by visiting your Search Personalization settings, where you remain in control of your data and can adjust your preferences at any time.

We are adding Google Wallet and Google Drive to Personal Intelligence to provide more relevant search results.

You can now connect your financial data to identify spending habits and optimize your credit card rewards.

Connecting your documents allows you to receive personalized plans based on information across your various files.

You remain in control of your data by choosing which apps to connect and managing your settings.

Robby Stein, VP of Product for Google Search, explains that you can now connect your apps like Google Wallet and Drive to Search for more personalized results. When you opt in, Search uses your own documents, spending habits, and recent activity to provide tailored answers. This helps you track financial goals, organize project information, and continue research tasks without repeating yourself. You remain in control and can manage these connections in your settings at any time.

The most helpful search experience brings together the richness of the world’s information with insights uniquely relevant to you. Today, Search is getting even more tailored with the ability to connect more of your apps to Personal Intelligence — and we're introducing more personally relevant responses, so it's easier to find just what you need.

Starting to roll out today, you can opt in to securely connect Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, with support for Drive and the Gemini app following in the coming weeks — bringing context from your spending, documents, and chats directly to Search. These apps join Gmail, Calendar, and Photos in delivering even more tailored responses with your personal context.

Get a clearer picture of your spending with Google Wallet: By connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence in both AI Mode and the Gemini app, you can map out your financial milestones and identify actionable ways to trim everyday spending. You can also maximize credit card benefits — like optimizing cash-back categories, travel perks, and reward points — based on your cards linked via Wallet. If you choose to connect your Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from your accounts; it can’t move, manage, or invest your money.

Stay in your flow with Google Drive: Sometimes the important information that you need to get started on a project or make a big decision can be scattered across your docs, sheets, or PDFs. With Google Drive connected in Personal Intelligence, you can get uniquely helpful responses that take all of that context into account and help you get started, like a personalized preparation plan ahead of tax season.

Connect the dots between the Gemini app and Search: In the coming weeks you can easily share context across the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search. So if you explore an idea in the Gemini app, AI Mode will have that foundation to build on, and vice versa. While you could already opt in to connect your Search history to Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app, soon you can also opt in to securely connect your Gemini app to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode.

To connect your apps to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, open Search Personalization, select Connected Apps, and then choose the apps you want to connect. You choose if and when you opt in, and you can turn those connections on or off at any time. You’re always in control of your personalization settings, and soon you’ll also be able to view the context AI Mode uses via the “Personalization” icon below any tailored response. If you want to edit anything simply let AI Mode know what to change, like responding in thread “I’m no longer a vegetarian.”

You’ll also start seeing more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode, tailored to your recent search context. So if you’ve been researching and planning for a trip, you can pick up right where you left off in a new search thread without starting over or repeating yourself. As always, you can adjust or turn off personalization at any time in your Search Settings.

items.body_ko: Google Wallet, Drive, 그리고 Gemini 앱을 AI Mode의 Personal Intelligence에 안전하게 연결하도록 선택하여 더욱 유용한 검색 응답을 얻으세요.브라우저가 오디오 요소를 지원하지 않습니다.Google Wallet과 Drive를 Personal Intelligence에 추가하여 검색이 사용자의 지출, 문서 및 채팅을 기반으로 답변을 제공할 수 있도록 합니다. 이러한 업데이트는 재정 관리를 돕고, 프로젝트를 정리하며, 검색 스레드 전반에 걸쳐 컨텍스트를 유지하는 데 도움이 됩니다. 검색 개인화 설정(Search Personalization settings)을 방문하여 이러한 앱을 연결하도록 선택할 수 있으며, 이 곳에서 데이터에 대한 통제권을 유지하고 언제든지 환경설정을 조정할 수 있습니다.더욱 관련성 높은 검색 결과를 제공하기 위해 Google Wallet과 Google Drive를 Personal Intelligence에 추가하고 있습니다.이제 재무 데이터를 연결하여 지출 습관을 파악하고 신용카드 혜택을 최적화할 수 있습니다.문서를 연결하면 다양한 파일의 정보를 기반으로 맞춤형 계획을 받을 수 있습니다.연결할 앱을 선택하고 설정을 관리하여 데이터에 대한 통제권을 유지합니다.Google Search의 제품 부사장인 Robby Stein은 이제 Google Wallet 및 Drive와 같은 앱을 검색에 연결하여 더욱 개인화된 결과를 얻을 수 있다고 설명합니다. 사용자가 동의하면 검색은 자신의 문서, 지출 습관 및 최근 활동을 사용하여 맞춤형 답변을 제공합니다. 이는 재정 목표를 추적하고, 프로젝트 정보를 정리하며, 반복 없이 연구 작업을 계속하는 데 도움이 됩니다. 사용자는 통제권을 유지하며 언제든지 설정에서 이러한 연결을 관리할 수 있습니다.가장 유용한 검색 경험은 전 세계 정보의 풍부함과 사용자에게 고유하게 관련된 통찰력을 결합합니다. 오늘날 검색은 더 많은 앱을 Personal Intelligence에 연결하는 기능으로 더욱 맞춤화되고 있으며, 더 개인적으로 관련성 높은 응답을 도입하여 필요한 것을 더 쉽게 찾을 수 있도록 합니다.오늘부터 순차적으로 Google Wallet을 AI Mode의 Personal Intelligence에 안전하게 연결하도록 선택할 수 있으며, Drive 및 Gemini 앱 지원은 몇 주 내에 제공될 예정입니다. 이를 통해 사용자의 지출, 문서 및 채팅의 컨텍스트를 검색으로 직접 가져옵니다. 이러한 앱은 Gmail, Calendar 및 Photos와 함께 개인적인 컨텍스트를 통해 더욱 맞춤화된 응답을 제공합니다.Google Wallet으로 지출에 대한 명확한 그림을 얻으세요: Google Wallet을 AI Mode 및 Gemini 앱의 Personal Intelligence에 연결하면 재무 목표를 계획하고 일상 지출을 줄일 수 있는 실행 가능한 방법을 식별할 수 있습니다. 또한 Wallet을 통해 연결된 카드를 기반으로 캐시백 카테고리, 여행 혜택 및 보상 포인트와 같은 신용카드 혜택을 극대화할 수 있습니다. Wallet 연결을 선택하더라도 AI Mode는 계정의 정보만 읽을 수 있으며, 돈을 이동, 관리 또는 투자할 수 없습니다.Google Drive로 흐름을 유지하세요: 때때로 프로젝트를 시작하거나 중요한 결정을 내리는 데 필요한 중요한 정보가 문서, 시트 또는 PDF에 흩어져 있을 수 있습니다. Gemini 앱에서 검색 기록을 Personal Intelligence에 연결하도록 이미 선택할 수 있었지만, 곧 Gemini 앱을 AI Mode의 Personal Intelligence에 안전하게 연결하도록 선택할 수도 있습니다.앱을 AI Mode의 Personal Intelligence에 연결하려면 검색 개인화(Search Personalization)를 열고 연결된 앱(Connected Apps)을 선택한 다음 연결하려는 앱을 선택하세요. 사용자는 연결 여부와 시점을 선택하며, 언제든지 이러한 연결을 켜거나 끌 수 있습니다. 개인화 설정은 항상 사용자가 통제하며, 곧 맞춤형 응답 아래의 “개인화” 아이콘을 통해 AI Mode가 사용하는 컨텍스트를 볼 수 있게 됩니다. 변경할 사항이 있으면 스레드에서 “나는 더 이상 채식주의자가 아닙니다”와 같이 AI Mode에 알려주세요.또한 AI 개요(AI Overviews) 및 AI Mode에서 최근 검색 컨텍스트에 맞춰 더 개인적으로 관련성 높은 응답을 보게 될 것입니다. 따라서 여행을 조사하고 계획했다면, 새로운 검색 스레드에서 처음부터 다시 시작하거나 반복할 필요 없이 중단했던 부분부터 바로 이어서 할 수 있습니다. 언제든지 검색 설정(Search Settings)에서 개인화를 조정하거나 끌 수 있습니다.Google의 최신 뉴스를 받은 편지함에서 확인하세요제품 업데이트, 이벤트 정보, 특별 제안 등이 포함된 뉴스레터를 구독하세요.구독을 확인하려면 받은 편지함을 확인하세요. .을(를) 사용하여 구독할 수도 있습니다.사용자 정보는 Google의 개인정보처리방침에 따라 사용됩니다. 언제든지 거부할 수 있습니다.

items.title: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation
items.body:
AI evaluations help shape which systems people build, adopt, and trust. An evaluation gives a system tasks, checks its answers or actions, and produces a score. Building and maintaining a useful evaluation therefore takes real work: defining tasks that reflect domain expertise, scoring them reliably, and checking that the results support the claims made. When methods, code, and data stay private, that work is harder for others to scrutinize or build on.

Open source offers a means to build stronger, more frequently updated, and more comparable evaluations and the infrastructure around them. Existing tasks, environments, and tools give builders a starting point, so their effort can go to domain expertise and validation. Sharing how an evaluation was built, including what went wrong, lets others find errors, improve it, and reuse it.

The Hugging Face hub is the home for AI evaluation: we host around 3500 eval leaderboards and have seen about a 16X growth in eval datasets on the hub in the past year, to about 17000 datasets. In recent months, we have also incorporated support for agentic abstractions that are relevant to evaluation. For example, Traces that store an agent’s work in an easily reviewable and sharable way; Benchmarks that highlight datasets used to evaluate models with leaderboards; and Environments that show datasets used as agentic RL or evaluation environments.

This guide covers four things:

Three eras of evaluation (section 1). Evaluations moved from checking answers, to checking what an agent did, to checking what a team of agents produces. Each step adds software that can change the score.

The steps in an agentic evaluation (section 2). We follow one task through eight steps, from the claim to the reported score. The full walkthrough, with commands, is in Appendix A.

When a benchmark is wrong (section 3). Errors in tasks and graders are common. We look at how they are found and corrected.

What to open strategically and why (section 4). A table sets out, component by component, what to share and what can stay protected.

In the research community, AI evaluation terminology is notoriously inconsistent. The glossary at the end defines each term we use and notes the other names you may come across.

1. Introduction: how evaluation design has changed

AI evaluation design has evolved in three forms as language models have become more capable and able to perform more complex work: question answer, agentic, and teams or swarms. Question-answer benchmarks such as MMLU (2020) and GPQA (2023) measure knowledge and reasoning through the answers models produce. As models became capable of planning and using tools, agentic benchmarks such as SWE-bench and WebArena expanded the scope to resolving software issues and completing tasks on websites. These tasks require evaluation setups that account for the environment in which the system operates and the changes it makes.

Lately, research on multi-agent systems has started to add another dimension: how agents coordinate and what they accomplish together. This includes decentralized swarms, teams managed by an orchestrator, and specialized agents collaborating on scientific work. Figure 1 shows a rough timeline of these three eras of evaluations.

Figure 1. Three types of language model evals. Question-and-answer benchmarks check a response against a key. Agentic benchmarks check what an agent changed in an environment. Team and swarm benchmarks score what a group of agents produced.

We’ll focus on agentic evaluations in this article for two reasons. First, they are becoming increasingly the most prominent type in model release announcements due to high user and enterprise interest in agentic deployment. Second, they offer a useful starting point for understanding how evaluation design affects model performance. Team and swarm evaluations introduce further complexity through interactions between agents, which we leave outside the scope of this guide. Once an agent uses tools to complete a task, each part of the surrounding software can affect its score. For instance, in an audit of Terminal-Bench, researchers kept the model fixed and changed the agent harness. Accuracy varied by up to 29.9 percentage points. To understand differences like that, we examine the anatomy of an agentic evaluation and follow one task from the instructions the agent receives to the checks that determine whether it passed.

The anatomy of an agentic evaluation

Figure 2. The different components of an agentic evaluation.

There are various parts to an agentic evaluation. A task gives the agent its instruction. The agent harness wraps the model and its tools, letting it work inside a pinned environment. During one rollout, the agent attempts the task from start to finish: it may run several commands, inspect their output, and try again before it stops. The evaluation harness runs several rollouts for each task. When a rollout ends, the verifier grades the environment's final state. Each rollout also leaves a trace, and traces and scores together become part of the final published evidence. Each part can be published, inspected, and reused separately.

Why benchmark release decisions matter

Demand for independent evaluation is growing. Policymakers, enterprises, and researchers want evaluations they can verify, and today they mostly cannot: 98.2% of model-benchmark scores are reported by only one party, and researchers have argued that in-house evaluation is not enough.

At the same time, more benchmarks are holding back test items to reduce contamination: questions or solutions entering training data, so scores may reflect prior exposure. Artificial Analysis says 60% of its Intelligence Index v5, announced in October 2026, rests on evaluations with private test sets or held-out answers. Google DeepMind recently piloted double-blind evaluations, where a secure enclave hides an outside evaluator's test prompts from the model provider and the model's weights from the evaluator. While that can reduce contamination, privacy by itself does not guarantee quality, and withholding supporting materials can make expert review harder. We argue that builders can and should still share infrastructure, grading methods, and evidence about task design. Scrutiny depends on giving others a way to question the measurement and correct mistakes, including controlled review where public release is unsuitable.

2. Building an eval: what to reuse, adapt, and validate

With the anatomy in place, we now build one agentic evaluation for a real use case: an agent that analyzes measurements for a physics lab. Rather than starting from scratch, we adapt an open task, so most of our effort goes into domain expertise and validation.

We work through eight steps: define the claim, find a task, run it unchanged, adapt it, check the evaluation, read the traces, report the score, and compare models. We then take stock of what we reused. The full walkthrough is in Appendix A. Figure 3 maps the steps and what each produced in our example.

Figure 3. The eight steps of building an agentic evaluation. The left panel highlights each step in turn, and the right panel shows what it involved in our example. Yellow steps work on the evaluation itself, and orange steps run models and read the results.

AI 평가는 사람들이 어떤 시스템을 구축하고 채택하며 신뢰하는지에 큰 영향을 미칩니다. 평가는 시스템에 작업을 부여하고, 그 응답이나 행동을 확인한 다음 점수를 산출합니다. 따라서 유용한 평가를 구축하고 유지하는 데는 상당한 노력이 필요합니다. 즉, 도메인 전문 지식을 반영하는 작업을 정의하고, 이를 안정적으로 채점하며, 결과가 제시된 주장을 뒷받침하는지 확인해야 합니다. 방법론, 코드, 데이터가 비공개로 유지되면 다른 사람들이 이를 검토하거나 기반으로 삼기 어렵습니다.

오픈 소스는 더 강력하고, 더 자주 업데이트되며, 더 비교 가능한 평가와 그 주변 인프라를 구축할 수 있는 수단을 제공합니다. 기존 작업, 환경, 도구는 개발자에게 시작점을 제공하여 그들의 노력이 도메인 전문성과 검증에 집중될 수 있도록 합니다. 평가가 어떻게 구축되었는지, 무엇이 잘못되었는지 등을 공유하면 다른 사람들이 오류를 찾아 개선하고 재사용할 수 있습니다.

Hugging Face Hub는 AI 평가의 본고장입니다. 우리는 약 3500개의 평가 리더보드를 호스팅하고 있으며, 지난 한 해 동안 Hub의 평가 데이터셋이 약 16배 증가하여 약 17000개에 달하는 것을 확인했습니다. 최근 몇 달 동안, 우리는 평가와 관련된 에이전트적 추상화에 대한 지원도 통합했습니다. 예를 들어, 에이전트의 작업을 쉽게 검토하고 공유할 수 있는 방식으로 저장하는 Traces, 리더보드를 통해 모델을 평가하는 데 사용되는 데이터셋을 강조하는 Benchmarks, 에이전트적 RL 또는 평가 환경으로 사용되는 데이터셋을 보여주는 Environments 등이 있습니다.

이 가이드에서는 네 가지 내용을 다룹니다.

평가의 세 가지 시대(섹션 1). 평가는 답변 확인에서 에이전트가 수행한 작업 확인으로, 그리고 에이전트 팀이 생산한 결과물 확인으로 변화했습니다. 각 단계마다 점수를 변경할 수 있는 소프트웨어가 추가됩니다.

에이전트적 평가의 단계(섹션 2). 우리는 하나의 작업을 주장부터 보고된 점수까지 8단계로 따라갑니다. 전체적인 단계별 설명과 명령어는 부록 A에 있습니다.

벤치마크가 잘못되었을 때(섹션 3). 작업과 채점자에서의 오류는 흔합니다. 이러한 오류가 어떻게 발견되고 수정되는지 살펴봅니다.

전략적으로 무엇을 공개하고 왜 공개해야 하는가(섹션 4). 표는 구성 요소별로 무엇을 공유하고 무엇을 보호할 수 있는지 설명합니다.

연구 커뮤니티에서 AI 평가 용어는 일관성이 없기로 악명이 높습니다. 마지막에 있는 용어집은 우리가 사용하는 각 용어를 정의하고 여러분이 접할 수 있는 다른 이름을 명시합니다.

1. 서론: 평가 설계의 변화

언어 모델이 더 유능해지고 더 복잡한 작업을 수행할 수 있게 됨에 따라 AI 평가 설계는 질문-답변, 에이전트적, 팀 또는 스웜의 세 가지 형태로 진화했습니다. MMLU(2020) 및 GPQA(2023)와 같은 질문-답변 벤치마크는 모델이 생성하는 답변을 통해 지식과 추론을 측정합니다. 모델이 계획하고 도구를 사용할 수 있게 되면서 SWE-bench 및 WebArena와 같은 에이전트적 벤치마크는 소프트웨어 문제 해결 및 웹사이트에서 작업 완료로 범위를 확장했습니다. 이러한 작업에는 시스템이 작동하는 환경과 시스템이 만드는 변경 사항을 설명하는 평가 설정이 필요합니다.

최근에는 다중 에이전트 시스템에 대한 연구가 또 다른 차원을 추가하기 시작했습니다. 즉, 에이전트가 어떻게 협력하고 무엇을 함께 달성하는지입니다. 여기에는 분산된 스웜, 오케스트레이터가 관리하는 팀, 과학 작업에 협력하는 전문 에이전트가 포함됩니다. 그림 1은 이러한 세 가지 평가 시대의 대략적인 타임라인을 보여줍니다.

그림 1. 언어 모델 평가의 세 가지 유형. 질문-답변 벤치마크는 답변을 키와 비교하여 확인합니다. 에이전트적 벤치마크는 에이전트가 환경에서 무엇을 변경했는지 확인합니다. 팀 및 스웜 벤치마크는 에이전트 그룹이 생산한 결과물을 채점합니다.

이 글에서는 두 가지 이유로 에이전트적 평가에 중점을 둘 것입니다. 첫째, 에이전트적 배포에 대한 높은 사용자 및 기업 관심으로 인해 모델 출시 발표에서 점점 더 가장 두드러진 유형이 되고 있습니다. 둘째, 평가 설계가 모델 성능에 어떻게 영향을 미치는지 이해하는 데 유용한 출발점을 제공합니다. 팀 및 스웜 평가는 에이전트 간의 상호 작용을 통해 추가적인 복잡성을 도입하며, 이는 이 가이드의 범위를 벗어납니다. 에이전트가 도구를 사용하여 작업을 완료하면 주변 소프트웨어의 각 부분이 점수에 영향을 미칠 수 있습니다. 예를 들어, Terminal-Bench 감사에서 연구원들은 모델을 고정하고 에이전트 하네스를 변경했습니다. 정확도는 최대 29.9%p까지 다양했습니다. 이러한 차이점을 이해하기 위해 우리는 에이전트적 평가의 구조를 조사하고 에이전트가 받는 지침부터 통과 여부를 결정하는 확인까지 하나의 작업을 따라갑니다.

에이전트적 평가의 구조

그림 2. 에이전트적 평가의 다양한 구성 요소.

에이전트적 평가에는 다양한 부분이 있습니다. 작업은 에이전트에게 지시를 내립니다. 에이전트 하네스는 모델과 그 도구를 감싸서 고정된 환경 내에서 작동하게 합니다. 한 번의 롤아웃 중에 에이전트는 작업을 처음부터 끝까지 시도합니다. 여러 명령을 실행하고, 그 출력을 검사하고, 멈추기 전에 다시 시도할 수 있습니다. 평가 하네스는 각 작업에 대해 여러 롤아웃을 실행합니다. 롤아웃이 끝나면 검증자가 환경의 최종 상태를 채점합니다. 각 롤아웃은 또한 흔적을 남기고, 흔적과 점수는 함께 최종 게시된 증거의 일부가 됩니다. 각 부분은 별도로 게시, 검사 및 재사용될 수 있습니다.

벤치마크 출시 결정이 중요한 이유

독립적인 평가에 대한 수요가 증가하고 있습니다. 정책 입안자, 기업 및 연구원들은 검증 가능한 평가를 원하지만 오늘날 대부분은 불가능합니다. 모델-벤치마크 점수의 98.2%가 단일 당사자에 의해 보고되며, 연구원들은 사내 평가만으로는 충분하지 않다고 주장합니다.

동시에, 더 많은 벤치마크가 오염을 줄이기 위해 테스트 항목을 보류하고 있습니다. 즉, 질문이나 솔루션이 훈련 데이터에 들어가 점수가 이전 노출을 반영할 수 있습니다. Artificial Analysis는 2026년 10월에 발표된 Intelligence Index v5의 60%가 비공개 테스트 세트 또는 보류된 답변이 있는 평가에 기반하고 있다고 말합니다. Google DeepMind는 최근 이중 맹검 평가를 시범 운영했는데, 여기서는 보안 인클레이브가 외부 평가자의 테스트 프롬프트를 모델 제공자와 모델의 가중치로부터 숨깁니다.

items.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
items.body:
GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer

GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this:

In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count.

This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th, who said:

Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality.

GLM 5.4 is not (yet?) available as open weights. I tried it out using the Z.ai API, for which I had to sign up for their Coding Plan subscription because 5.4 cannot currently be accessed through the regular API.

It turns out both coding plan and regular API share the same OpenAI-compatible Responses API (at https://api.z.ai/api/v1), and the API key for the coding plan worked with that and gave me access to the new model.

I built a llm-glm plugin, then realized that llm-zai by Tommy Hughes already exists! I've shipped mine purely because llm-zai doesn't yet support the new model, but I'll likely retire mine once that plugin catches up.

Here are pelicans for GLM-5.4 on low, high, and max. This is the max one:

I realized I never ran pelicans for GLM-5.3, so here those are for the same effort levels. They look similar in quality to 5.4.

It's interesting how GLM 5.1 and GLM 5.2 produced radically different pelicans from other models. The pelicans for 5.3 and 5.4 are much more comparable to those I get from OpenAI or Anthropic models - the previous generations had their own distinctive look.

I made a comparison grid showing the four generations of GLM pelicans all in one place. The style transition between 5.2 and 5.3 is pretty stark.

items.title: When Does Fine-Tuning Beat Prompting for Qiskit-to-CUDA-Q Translation? An Execution-Verified Study
items.body: Moving quantum code from Qiskit to NVIDIA CUDA-Q is a practical adoption cost that language models are starting to automate. We ask whether a small open model can learn this translation, and how to measure it so that the result can be trusted. Both programs can be executed and their state vectors compared, so a kernel counts as correct only if it prepares the same state as the Qiskit reference (fidelity >= 0.999), with no text matching and no LLM judge. We build a 640-task benchmark with three test sets (larger circuits, an unseen circuit family, an unseen Qiskit coding style) and a QuantumKatas regression probe, and we test the evaluator before training. Measurement counts miss every phase-only error; a surface rule-based translator solves two of three original splits (text substitution); a converter that executes the Qiskit input and maps the circuit solves all 640 tasks -- so the benchmark measures source-level translation, not whether a circuit can be ported after running it. No base model emits a valid CUDA-Q kernel zero-shot. On Nemotron 3 Nano 4B, LoRA reaches 83.9%, tying a 4-shot prompt (83.1%), but generalizes worse to unseen style (48.5% vs. 65.5%) and cuts QuantumKatas from 23.8% to 8.9%; on Qwen2.5-Coder 7B, LoRA beats the prompt overall (92.0% vs. 82.8%) and on unseen style (78.5% vs. 65.0%), and on the 1.5B model as well, so whether fine-tuning pays off depends on the base model, while the Qiskit regression appears in all three. Mixing two replay formats is the best mitigation trade-off (84.4% translation, Katas 21.5%). On 48 parametric functions that must become kernels with arguments -- where executing the input cannot yield a parametric kernel -- models reach up to 83%; on 27 real QED-C kernels, every model scores 0%. Language models can do source-level translation of simple parametric code, but not yet of real programs.
items.body_ko: Qiskit 코드를 NVIDIA CUDA-Q로 옮기는 것은 언어 모델이 자동화하기 시작한 실질적인 채택 비용입니다. 우리는 작은 오픈 모델이 이러한 번역을 학습할 수 있는지, 그리고 그 결과를 신뢰할 수 있도록 측정하는 방법을 묻습니다. 두 프로그램 모두 실행할 수 있으며 해당 상태 벡터를 비교할 수 있으므로, 커널은 Qiskit 참조와 동일한 상태를 준비하는 경우에만 올바른 것으로 간주됩니다(충실도 >= 0.999). 텍스트 일치 또는 LLM 심사위원은 없습니다. 우리는 세 가지 테스트 세트(더 큰 회로, 보지 못한 회로군, 보지 못한 Qiskit 코딩 스타일)와 QuantumKatas 회귀 프로브를 포함하는 640개 작업 벤치마크를 구축하고, 훈련 전에 평가기를 테스트합니다. 측정 횟수는 모든 위상 전용 오류를 놓칩니다. 표면 규칙 기반 번역기는 세 가지 원래 분할 중 두 가지를 해결합니다(텍스트 대체). Qiskit 입력을 실행하고 회로를 매핑하는 변환기는 640개 작업을 모두 해결합니다. 따라서 벤치마크는 회로를 실행한 후 이식할 수 있는지 여부가 아니라 소스 수준 번역을 측정합니다. 어떤 기본 모델도 유효한 CUDA-Q 커널을 제로샷으로 내보내지 않습니다. Nemotron 3 Nano 4B에서 LoRA는 83.9%에 도달하여 4샷 프롬프트(83.1%)와 동률을 이루지만, 보지 못한 스타일에 대한 일반화는 더 나빴고(48.5% 대 65.5%) QuantumKatas는 23.8%에서 8.9%로 감소했습니다. Qwen2.5-Coder 7B에서 LoRA는 전반적으로 프롬프트를 능가했으며(92.0% 대 82.8%) 보지 못한 스타일에서도 능가했습니다(78.5% 대 65.0%). 1.5B 모델에서도 마찬가지였습니다. 따라서 파인튜닝의 효과는 기본 모델에 따라 달라지며, Qiskit 회귀는 세 가지 모두에서 나타났습니다. 두 가지 리플레이 형식을 혼합하는 것이 최상의 완화 절충점입니다(84.4% 번역, Katas 21.5%). 인수를 가진 커널이 되어야 하는 48개의 매개변수 함수(입력을 실행해도 매개변수 커널을 생성할 수 없는 경우)에서 모델은 최대 83%에 도달합니다. 27개의 실제 QED-C 커널에서는 모든 모델이 0%를 기록합니다. 언어 모델은 간단한 매개변수 코드의 소스 수준 번역은 가능하지만, 실제 프로그램은 아직 불가능합니다.

items.title: A Cascaded Framework with a Cross-Attention-Guided Mamba-CNN Model for Pre- and Post-Treatment Glioma Segmentation
items.body: Accurate glioma segmentation is vital for diagnosis and follow-up, but manual segmentation is time-consuming, subjective, and variable across interpreters. Gliomas are heterogeneous in size, shape, and location. Deep learning has therefore emerged as a potential solution. CNNs excel at local features but may struggle with long-range dependencies, whereas Vision Transformers capture global context efficiently but incur higher computational complexity. Most previous studies focused on pre-treatment gliomas; post-treatment cases with resection cavities (RCs) remain less explored. This study proposes a Cross-Attention-Guided Mamba-CNN (CMC-Seg) model within a cascaded framework for pre- and post-treatment diffuse glioma segmentation, aiming to balance accuracy and computational cost. Experiments used BraTS 2025 mpMRI of diffuse glioma patients. After preprocessing, a coarse segmentation model extracted tumor-centered patches, which were fed to CMC-Seg for fine-grained segmentation. CMC-Seg was compared with 3D U-Net, SegResNet, SwinUNETR, UNETR, nnFormer, and SegMamba. On the test set, CMC-Seg achieved the highest mean Dice (81.20%) and non-enhancing tumor core (NETC) Dice (77.09%). It also achieved an RC Dice of 78.63% and the lowest 95% Hausdorff distance (HD95; 4.39 mm). Results were comparable to CNN and Mamba baselines and significantly better than Transformer-based baselines (P < 0.05). CMC-Seg required the fewest inference GFLOPs (381.49). Ablation experiments indicated that multi-direction scanning and cross-attention improved performance, particularly for RC (P < 0.05). Grad-CAM explainability experiments showed that CMC-Seg focuses on diagnostically relevant tumor regions.

items.title: Tabular Foundation Models for Weighted Regression and Classification
items.body: Weighted regression and classification have applications ranging from missing-data analysis and causal inference to insurance pricing and particle physics. Existing weighted methods must be fitted and tuned on each dataset, which is costly for flexible nonlinear learners. Tabular foundation models avoid this cost. A Transformer is pretrained once on many simulated datasets and then predicts on a new dataset by in-context learning, using its observations as context without further fitting. Recent models such as TabPFN-3.5 surpass tuned conventional methods, but they cannot use sample weights. We develop a general pipeline that adapts such models to weighted prediction through weighted attention, a normalized weighted loss, and pretraining on synthetic weighted prediction tasks from missing-data problems. Applied to TabPFN-3.5, it yields WeightedPFN, which performs strongly on real datasets, both in missing-data problems and in out-of-distribution causal tasks, while running about as fast as linear baselines. We also establish a statistical theory showing that a suitably pretrained weighted Transformer attains the nonparametric minimax rate for weighted regression on new datasets without further fitting.

items.title: Constrained Diffusion from Binary Evaluations via Learned Doob h-Functions
items.body: Conditional generation under constraints that can only be checked on a finished sample, such as a molecular property filter, remains challenging for diffusion models: most guidance methods require differentiable measurement operators, paired conditional data, or rollouts of the base model at every step. We present a framework grounded in the Doob $h$-transform that reduces conditional generation to learning a single function, the probability that a noisy sample denoises into the constraint set. We learn this function from binary clean-sample evaluations alone, by squared-error regression on forward-noised labels; the base model is frozen, one lightweight head is trained per constraint, and noisy-state classifier guidance arises as a special case. The exact guidance step fades where the constraint signal provably vanishes and carries a factor of the inverse probability across samples, which normalized guidance discards: with the schedule and mean step size held fixed, equalizing the step costs 17.0 to 18.5 points of constraint satisfaction on CIFAR-10 at comparable FID, across independently trained estimators. Guidance is more than 50$\times$ cheaper per satisfying sample than rejection sampling at a 1.7% base rate, raises a Lipinski-type property filter on QM9 from 54.3% to 96.8%, and lifts satisfaction on Stable Diffusion 1.5 from 7.2% to 60.0% at one sixteenth of the cost of derivative-free selection, which reaches 9.0%. These results demonstrate that binary evaluations of clean samples are sufficient supervision for constrained generation across pixel, latent, and molecular diffusion.

items.title: ComplexIF: A Challenging Multi-Turn, Multi-Constraint Instruction-Following Benchmark
items.body: As frontier LLMs saturate existing instruction-following benchmarks, measuring further progress requires harder tests that remain faithful to real use. In practice, users often combine several constraints, add them at different turns of a conversation, and expect all of them to hold in the assistant's response. We introduce ComplexIF, a challenging benchmark for this setting, together with the automatic pipeline that generates it. The pipeline expands seed requests into multi-turn conversations, weaves constraints into their turns, and keeps only tasks that a strong model can solve, so difficulty can be raised by adding constraints or turns while every task stays solvable. ComplexIF's two splits test complementary sides of instruction following: a verifiable split of format constraints, checked by programs, and a rubric split of semantic instructions, such as a tone or an audience, checked with an LLM judge. Across 14 proprietary and open-weight models, even the strongest satisfies every constraint on fewer than half of the verifiable tasks, and no model leads on both splits.

items.title: S1Arena-MM: Which Multimodal Decisions Can Be Left to System 1?
items.body: Perception systems often make discrete decisions: flag a hateful meme, predict whether a pedestrian will cross, detect a spoofed voice, or select the next move in a game. System-1 models, such as OneJev and Jev-Omni, read the media and return probabilities over the options in a single forward pass, while multimodal large language models (MLLMs) generate text. Which multimodal decisions can System-1 models handle, and where do MLLMs perform better? We introduce S1Arena-MM, a benchmark that gives every model the same decision requests and scores the probabilities it returns. It contains 51,060 questions across 94 tasks with image, video, and audio input, drawn from 94 public datasets and three program-generated ones. It also includes 102 closed-loop game environments that a model plays from screenshots; in real-time mode, the game continues while the model decides. We evaluate 33 open models: 12 System-1 models and 21 MLLMs read at the answer token. On static decisions, the best System-1 model leads the best MLLM by 4.9 percentage points on images and is within one point of it on video and audio. Post-training for decisions mainly improves the probabilities: on video, a System-1 model has a lower Brier score than the MLLM that it is post-trained from in 10 of 12 pairs. With up to 2,048 thought tokens per question, the most accurate MLLMs pass the best System-1 models only slightly, and thinking raises the Brier score of most MLLMs. Closed loops separate the models: three System-1 models built on a 27B MLLM reach 22.0-33.3% progression in BALROG, and no other model exceeds 9.7% with thinking off. In real-time GameWorld, latencies of up to 1.1 s per decision cause no measurable loss of progress for System-1 models. Code and data: https://github.com/zhaoyang02/S1Arena-MM.

items.summary_ko: S1Arena-MM은 멀티모달 의사 결정 문제에서 System-1 모델(단일 포워드 패스로 확률 반환)과 멀티모달 대규모 언어 모델(MLLM, 텍스트 생성)의 성능을 비교하는 벤치마크입니다. 어떤 유형의 멀티모달 결정에 System-1 모델이 적합하고, MLLM이 더 나은 성능을 보이는지 평가합니다.

items.title: Into My Arms: Structured reinforcement learning for autonomous transport of objects and humans
items.body: Whole-body humanoid manipulation remains bottlenecked by high-dimensional state-action spaces, contact-rich environments, and long task horizons. This trilemma is a challenge that state-of-the-art reinforcement learning (RL) methods are yet to resolve reliably. We address it with three contributions that add just enough structure to guide exploration: Sparse Interaction Edges (SIE) for whole-body manipulation, Interaction Gated Transport (IGT) for sustained transport over long horizons, and a Hinted Object Path (HOP) that resolves collision and search complexity bottlenecks. Across all three, the policy remains free to discover its own manipulation strategy. The method generalises from rigid object to human transport. As a flagship demonstration, we show, to our knowledge, the first bed-to-wheelchair transfer of a medical mannequin by a humanoid robot completed with no human intervention during execution. In the domain of human transfer, we show that a single policy can adapt across substantial variations in body mass, size, and random force perturbations, all while training on a single GPU in under an hour. Our approach offers a pathway to fully RL-driven humanoid manipulation, enabling assistive robots that can help humans. Website: https://elle-miller.github.io/into_my_arms

items.title: When Simpler Beats Learned: Dual-Weighted Sampling vs. Machine Learning for the Pricing Subproblem in Graph Coloring
items.body: The graph coloring problem can be solved to optimality by branch-and-price (B&P), but its performance hinges on the column generation (CG) step, where each iteration requires solving a maximum weight independent set (MWIS) pricing problem. The state-of-the-art machine-learning (ML) pricing heuristic follows a prediction-sampling paradigm: a learned model scores each vertex of a graph, and independent sets are sampled from the induced distribution. We observe, however, that the scoring procedure does not need to be learned, and critically assess the role of ML by replacing the learned scores with the dual solution of the restricted master problem, resulting in Dual-Weighted Sampling, a proposed lightweight alternative that requires no feature engineering or training. Within a unified CG and B&P framework that varies only the pricing oracle, Dual-Weighted Sampling outperforms MLPH, hand-crafted heuristics, and exact solvers on the established graph coloring benchmark in both runtime and solution quality. In particular, it remains competitive on the DIMACS random family, where MLPH was shown strongest in the original evaluation, while achieving more than a two-fold speedup in CG runtime on recursive-sparse and real-world graph families.
items.title_ko: 단순한 기법이 학습된 모델을 능가할 때: 그래프 색칠 문제의 가격 결정 하위 문제에서 듀얼 가중 샘플링 vs 머신러닝

items.title: Estimating a Transition Point from Gibbs and Ground States
items.body:
We study how observed many-body system size affects the number of state copies needed to estimate a zero-temperature first-order transition point. The unknown Hamiltonian has bounded, translation-invariant on-site and nearest-neighbour interactions on a 3D cubic lattice with local dimension three. The field coupling is known, and all models share a known boundary field penalizing one local level. The limiting order parameter is uniformly separated across the transition. Each query returns an independently prepared Gibbs or ground state at an adaptive field and system size.
For error $ε$ and fixed confidence, we prove an exponential separation between two size caps at the same temperature. There are absolute constants $00$ such that, at inverse temperature $β=c_1/ε$, restricting side lengths to $L\le c_0/ε$ requires $\exp(Ω(1/ε))$ copies in worst-case expectation, even with collective measurements. Allowing $L\le C/ε$ permits $O(\log^2(1/ε))$ copies and $O(ε^{-3})$ total spins, using local measurements and polynomial classical postprocessing. The minimax expected total spin count is $Θ(ε^{-3})$ uniformly for $β\ge c_1/ε$. At fixed positive temperature it is $Θ_β(ε^{-2})$, attained from one- and eight-site Gibbs states followed by exponential classical computation. For ground-state copies it is $Θ(ε^{-3})$.
The lower bound uses a three-state ferromagnet whose boundary suppresses the sector carrying transition information. A spanning-forest argument and edge-boundary counting control its Gibbs weight uniformly over fields and allowed sizes, and a trace-distance hybrid argument handles adaptive learners with quantum memory. The upper bound combines finite-volume free-energy estimates, concavity and local order-parameter measurements.

items.title: Sánchez, Feijóo, or Abascal? Speaker Attribution and Ideological Congruence in LLM Personas Reading Posts on X of the Leaders of the Three Main Parties of the 29N General Election in Spain
items.body: Source cues are central to political communication, yet reception studies with large language model (LLM) personas as synthetic audiences have not tested whether personas respond to who speaks and not only to what is said. With Spain's general election of 29 November 2026 in mind, we run a speaker-attribution experiment using 1,075 anonymised X posts by the leaders of PSOE, PP and VOX on four topics (the economy and employment, household costs, immigration and corruption) and 791 distinct value-grounded, LLM-generated personas. Each post was assigned to 300 topic-selected persona profiles, 150 grounded in the Inglehart-Welzel cultural map and 150 in Moral Foundations Theory, under four conditions: no author, Sánchez, Feijóo or Abascal, yielding 322,470 complete persona-post quartets. Naming any leader lowered support for identical text, with the penalty for Abascal nearly twice as large as those for Sánchez and Feijóo. The penalty follows the persona's elicited left-right self-placement (ideological congruence): left personas spare Sánchez and right personas spare Feijóo, although ideology was never in the message-evaluation prompt. Corruption posts were penalised under every name, whereas on other topics the ideologically closest leader generally produced little or no penalty. The leader order matches public opinion in 48 CIS barometers (2022-2026) in all three groups and the sign of all twelve differences, but fits barometers before the model's 2024 knowledge cutoff better than recent ones. Our findings demonstrate that LLM personas evaluate political speakers through systematic, value-congruent priors: however, while they replicate human candidate rank-orders across survey barometers, this alignment is ordinal rather than quantitative, highlighting their utility for controlled source-effect experiments though not as substitutes for empirical public opinion surveys.
items.title_ko: 스페인 총선 관련 LLM 페르소나의 화자 귀인 및 이데올로기 일치 분석
items.summary_ko: 스페인 총선 주요 정당 리더들의 X(구 트위터) 게시물을 LLM 페르소나에게 읽게 하여, 화자 귀인(speaker attribution) 능력과 이데올로기적 일치도를 분석하는 실험입니다. LLM 페르소나가 단순히 내용뿐만 아니라 '누가 말했는지'에도 반응하는지 테스트합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 단순한 텍스트 내용 외에 발화자의 맥락적 정보(화자 귀인)를 얼마나 인식하고 반응하는지 탐구하여, 정치 커뮤니케이션 분석 및 AI의 사회적 영향 이해에 기여합니다.

items.title: Selecting Stable Sampling Dynamics for Compositional Diffusion: A Feynman-Kac Weight Reduction
items.body: Given $K$ separately trained diffusion models, how should one sample from a $β_k$-weighted product of their terminal laws without jointly retraining the experts? Existing Feynman--Kac constructions provide many weighted stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with the correct target marginal. The consequential question is how to select useful proposal dynamics among them. We study an explicit family of weighted diffusions that realizes the same product-of-intermediate-experts trajectory. A scalar parameter $λ$ controls how strongly the proposal drift follows the composed expert score, while an additional Langevin component can be varied independently. Writing $B=\sum_{k=1}^{K}β_k>0$, we identify the distinguished choice $λ=1/B$. At this value, the aggregate squared-score term in the instantaneous Feynman--Kac log-weight rate cancels exactly. For positive expert exponents, the remaining score-disagreement contribution is non-positive. We call this structural cancellation Feynman--Kac reduction. Under bounded-divergence assumptions, it yields an upper bound on the instantaneous unnormalized log-weight rate for all $λ\leq 1/B$. For linear diffusion protocols with compactly supported expert data, $λ=1/B$ yields two-sided bounds at every nonterminal time, for exponents of either sign. A corresponding result holds for a single expert under the same divergence assumption. In these two-sided settings, the selected value is unique within the specified family in a universal worst-case sense. Experiments on Gaussian mixtures and molecular sampling compare the analytically predicted stability with actual sampling quality, including instances in which parameter choices different from $λ=1/B$ perform better empirically.
items.title_ko: 합성 확산을 위한 안정적인 샘플링 동역학 선택: Feynman-Kac 가중치 감소
items.summary_ko: K개의 독립적으로 훈련된 확산 모델에서 가중치 부여된 터미널 분포의 곱에서 샘플링하는 방법을 연구합니다. 기존 Feynman-Kac 구성은 올바른 목표 주변 분포를 가진 많은 확률 미분 방정식(SDE)을 제공하지만, 이 연구는 그중 유용한 제안 동역학을 선택하는 방법을 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: 여러 확산 모델을 효과적으로 결합하여 복잡한 분포에서 샘플링하는 방법을 개선하여, 고품질 데이터 생성 및 멀티모달 모델링 발전에 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: probly: Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning
items.body: As machine learning systems are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, the question of how to represent and quantify uncertainty has moved from a methodological side issue to a central concern. In practice, however, making a model uncertainty-aware is still surprisingly difficult: relevant tools tend to be scattered across libraries, each tied to a particular framework and a particular approach to modeling uncertainty, and the choice of representation, quantification, and evaluation is typically left to the user without much guidance. In this paper, we present probly, a Python package that addresses these issues in a single, modular framework. probly offers (i) lightweight transformations that turn existing models into uncertainty-aware ones, currently supporting PyTorch, scikit-learn, and Flax, (ii) several representations, including second-order distributions, credal sets, and conformal prediction, (iii) the corresponding quantification measures, and (iv) a number of evaluation protocols, which can be combined more or less arbitrarily. Using probly, we conduct a benchmark study on three standard tasks --- selective prediction, out-of-distribution detection, and active learning. In addition, and unlike existing benchmarks, we evaluate suitable methods on first-order data, i.e., datasets for which the target itself is a distribution over outcomes. We further illustrate the flexibility of the package on a number of less standard case studies, including large language models, graph neural networks, and data streams. The package is publicly available at https://github.com/pwhofman/probly.
items.body_ko: 머신러닝 시스템이 실제 애플리케이션에 점점 더 많이 배포됨에 따라, 불확실성을 표현하고 정량화하는 방법의 문제는 방법론적인 부수적인 문제에서 핵심적인 관심사로 바뀌었습니다. 그러나 실제로 모델을 불확실성 인식 모델로 만드는 것은 여전히 놀라울 정도로 어렵습니다. 관련 도구들은 라이브러리에 흩어져 있는 경향이 있으며, 각 라이브러리는 특정 프레임워크와 불확실성 모델링에 대한 특정 접근 방식에 묶여 있습니다. 그리고 표현, 정량화 및 평가의 선택은 일반적으로 많은 지침 없이 사용자에게 맡겨집니다. 본 논문에서는 이러한 문제들을 단일의 모듈식 프레임워크에서 해결하는 Python 패키지 probly를 소개합니다. probly는 (i) 기존 모델을 불확실성 인식 모델로 변환하는 경량 변환(현재 PyTorch, scikit-learn, Flax 지원), (ii) 2차 분포, 신념 집합 및 등각 예측을 포함한 여러 표현, (iii) 해당 정량화 측정, 그리고 (iv) 거의 임의로 결합할 수 있는 여러 평가 프로토콜을 제공합니다. probly를 사용하여 세 가지 표준 작업(선택적 예측, 분포 외 감지 및 능동 학습)에 대한 벤치마크 연구를 수행합니다. 또한 기존 벤치마크와 달리, 우리는 대상 자체가 결과에 대한 분포인 데이터셋, 즉 1차 데이터에 대해 적절한 방법을 평가합니다. 우리는 대규모 언어 모델, 그래프 신경망 및 데이터 스트림을 포함한 여러 가지 비표준 사례 연구에서 패키지의 유연성을 추가로 보여줍니다. 이 패키지는 https://github.com/pwhofman/probly에서 공개적으로 이용 가능합니다.
